cards.text: Jesus is still teaching His disciples about His coming (Matthew 24:3), and now He tells a story. The kingdom of heaven, He says, will be like ten virgins who take their lamps and go out to meet the bridegroom. Ten lamps, one bridegroom, and a WEDDING on the way!

cards.question: Jesus says the ten virgins aren't all alike. Five of them are foolish, and five are ___.

cards.text: The foolish ones take their lamps but no extra oil. That's starting a road trip with the gas light ALREADY on.

cards.question: The wise virgins do things differently. What do they bring along with their lamps?

cards.text: Then the bridegroom is delayed, and the waiting drags on. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, so trust me when I tell you waiting does something to people.

cards.question: While the bridegroom is delayed, only the foolish virgins get drowsy and fall asleep.

cards.text: Then at MIDNIGHT the cry rings out: "Here is the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!" Ten sleepy people, and just like that, it's GO time.

cards.question: The cry wakes up all ten virgins. What do they do with their lamps?

cards.text: Then the foolish ones look down, and their lamps are going out. That's the low battery beep, at MIDNIGHT, right when you need it most.

cards.question: With their lamps going out, the foolish virgins turn to the wise ones and ask them to give them some of their ___.
The wise virgins agree to share some of their oil with the foolish ones.
The wise virgins say no to sharing their oil. What reason do they give?

answers.text: There may not be enough for both
The bridegroom told them not to
The foolish ones should have planned

cards.question: Instead, the wise virgins tell the foolish ones to go to those who sell oil and buy some for themselves.

cards.text: So the foolish five head out to buy oil, at MIDNIGHT. You ever try to find anything open at midnight, friend? It's you, one gas station and a guy mopping.

cards.question: The bridegroom waits for the foolish virgins to get back with their oil before he goes in to the wedding banquet.
While the foolish virgins are away, those who are ready go in with the bridegroom to the wedding banquet, and the door is ___.

cards.text: Later the other virgins arrive and call out, "Lord, lord, open the door for us!" That's running up to the airport gate right after it closes, waving at a plane that is NOT coming back.

cards.question: The foolish virgins are outside the shut door, asking to be let in. What does the bridegroom reply?

answers.text: Truly I tell you I do not know you
Truly I tell you come back tomorrow
Truly I tell you there is no room

cards.question: Jesus ends the story by saying to keep watch. Why?

answers.text: You do not know the day or the hour
The bridegroom always comes at midnight
The night is almost over now

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now. Jesus isn't done teaching yet, friend, so keep that lamp handy.

findings.problem: Card 3 says the foolish virgins take their lamps but no extra oil. Card 4 then asks what the wise virgins bring along with their lamps. Once the baker reads card 3, the contrast makes 'Oil in flasks' obvious and rules out 'Water in jars' and 'Extra lamps', so the setup gives the answer away.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'So the foolish five head out to buy oil, at MIDNIGHT.' 'You ever try to find anything open at midnight, friend?' 'It's you, one gas station and a guy mopping.' Cards after the opening card can have only 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This card asks the baker to pick the bridegroom's exact reply. All three answers start with the same 'Truly I tell you' and differ only in the closing words. That tests whether the baker can guess the wording of the line, and nothing on the earlier cards lets them reason toward 'I do not know you' over the other refusals. The card should ask about what the reply means instead.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The junk drawer callback builds up and then stops with no punchline. 'Waiting does something to people' is a mild, pleasant remark, not a laugh. It reads like a nice dad being pleasant rather than laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: Card 20 contains only the line saying the teaching isn't done. It retells no verse, but it cites Matthew 25:13, which card 19 already asked about.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells no verse, what should its "verses" field cite? Should it be the passage's last verse, null, or something else?
